      112→def __getattr__(name):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
      113→    """PEP 562 lazy attribute access.
      114→
      115→    ``import hopsworks`` no longer triggers ``hsfs`` / ``hsml`` /
      116→    ``great_expectations``; the first time anyone reads
      117→    ``hopsworks.connection`` / ``hopsworks.udf`` / ``hopsworks.hsfs`` /
      118→    ``hopsworks.hsml``, the relevant module is imported and cached on the
      119→    package object so subsequent accesses are free.
      120→    """
      121→    factory = _LAZY.get(name)
      122→    if factory is None:
      123→        raise AttributeError(f"module 'hopsworks' has no attribute {name!r}")
      124→    value = factory()
      125→    # Cache so subsequent attribute lookups skip ``__getattr__`` entirely.
      126→    globals()[name] = value
      127→    return value
      128→
      129→
      130→# PEP 562 ``__getattr__`` only fires on attribute access, not when the import
      131→# machinery resolves a dotted module path. Without this finder,
      132→# ``from hopsworks.hsfs.builtin_transformations import X`` raises
      133→# ``ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hopsworks.hsfs'`` — the public
      134→# ``hopsworks.hsfs[.*]`` / ``hopsworks.hsml[.*]`` aliases have been supported
      135→# since #292 (Aug 2024) and downstream code (e.g. loadtest, customer notebooks)
      136→# depends on them. A meta-path finder restores the alias contract while keeping
      137→# the lazy goal: ``hsfs`` / ``hsml`` are only imported when something actually
      138→# references them, not on ``import hopsworks``.
      139→import importlib.util  # noqa: E402
      140→
      141→
      142→_ALIAS_TO_REAL = {"hopsworks.hsfs": "hsfs", "hopsworks.hsml": "hsml"}
      143→
      144→
      145→class _AliasLoader:
      146→    """No-op loader that hands back an already-executed module."""
      147→
      148→    def __init__(self, real_module):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
      149→        self._real = real_module
      150→
      151→    def create_module(self, spec):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
      152→        return self._real
      153→
      154→    def exec_module(self, module):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
      155→        pass  # real module was already executed by importlib.import_module
      156→
      157→
      158→class _HsfsHsmlAliasFinder:
      159→    """Route ``hopsworks.hsfs[.*]`` and ``hopsworks.hsml[.*]`` to the real packages."""
      160→
      161→    def find_spec(self, fullname, path=None, target=None):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
      162→        for alias, real in _ALIAS_TO_REAL.items():
      163→            if fullname == alias or fullname.startswith(alias + "."):
      164→                real_name = real + fullname[len(alias) :]
      165→                real_mod = importlib.import_module(real_name)
      166→                return importlib.util.spec_from_loader(fullname, _AliasLoader(real_mod))
      167→        return None
      168→
      169→
      170→# Append (not prepend) so the standard ``PathFinder`` and pytest's assertion
      171→# rewriter still run first for ordinary modules; our finder only fires for the
      172→# two alias namespaces, which no real on-disk subpackage shadows.
      173→if not any(isinstance(f, _HsfsHsmlAliasFinder) for f in sys.meta_path):
      174→    sys.meta_path.append(_HsfsHsmlAliasFinder())

      419→def _get_cached_api_key_path():
      420→    """This function is used to get an appropriate path to store the user supplied API Key for Hopsworks SaaS.
      421→
      422→    First it will search for .hw_api_key in the current working directory, if it exists it will use it (this is default in 3.0 client)
      423→    Otherwise, falls back to storing the API key in HOME
      424→    If not sufficient permissions are set in HOME to create the API key (writable and executable), it uses the temp directory to store it.
      425→    """
      426→    api_key_name = ".hw_api_key"
      427→    api_key_folder = f".{getpass.getuser()}_hopsworks_app"
      428→
      429→    # Path for current working directory api key
      430→    cwd_api_key_path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), api_key_name)
      431→
      432→    # Path for home api key
      433→    home_dir_path = os.path.expanduser("~")
      434→    home_api_key_path = os.path.join(home_dir_path, api_key_folder, api_key_name)
      435→
      436→    # Path for tmp api key
      437→    temp_dir_path = tempfile.gettempdir()
      438→    temp_api_key_path = os.path.join(temp_dir_path, api_key_folder, api_key_name)
      439→
      440→    if os.path.exists(
      441→        cwd_api_key_path
      442→    ):  # For backward compatibility, if .hw_api_key exists in current working directory get it from there
      443→        api_key_path = cwd_api_key_path
      444→    elif os.access(home_dir_path, os.W_OK) and os.access(

      448→    else:  # Finally try to store it in temp

      450→
      451→    return api_key_path
